notes.title: Day 4 : All games must patch!
notes.notes:
Ah, the days are rolling fast, and my fingers are aching from integrating all these lovely suggestions.

Here is a bunch of features implemented since yesterday:
- The suggestion system has been greatly improved, especially on the backend side.
- A "Thank you" screen has been designed, telling supporters when their suggestions have been implemented in the game.
- Optimized Case load time.
- Much needed spam/trolling defense on suggestions implemented.
- You can now hold down Shift to prevent words going black, designed mostly for suggestors.
- Successful suggestors are treated to a happy song when they log into a patch containing their suggestions.
- Added 3.000 lines of dialogue! 40% of it directly from player suggestions.
- Work on Chapter two is well underway.
- Fixed some scaling issues for rectangular displays.
- Fixed weird anti-aliasing issue on some retina macbooks.
- Fixed even more typos.
- Fixed some unintentional inconsistancies in some story archs.
- Fixed bug that would cause Red to completely ignore all user input.
- Added "cooling" effects, allowing certain sentences to reduce the breaking levels of the suspects.
- Fixed bug that could cause the camera to get stuck behind the suspects head.
- Fixed bug that would cause the police to talk with Mrs. Blue's voice.
- Added references to Auburn and Turquoise, characters from Episode 2 and 3.

That's all I got in the bag for today's patch. Tomorrow its going to be all about adding new features to help detectives keep track of statements, and better point out controversial/conflicting statements.

notes.title: Day 3 : Patch me outside!
notes.notes:
Since the weather is absolutely boiling today, I'm sitting mostly outside today, writing dialogue and fixing bugs. Here is the product of the day 3 harvest:

- Players can now type in parts of words, or type in the sentences they want, instead of having to look for the button.
- Added a whole lot of dialogue options. A lot-lot.
- Moved corkboard drawer key to the Tab key.
- The game will now run in the background, so alt-tabbing out and back in works.
- Adjustable text speed can be set in the settings menu.
- Adjustable UI scaling can be set in the settings menu.
- Improved support for Discord overlay.
- Improved support for Twitch overlay.
- Optimized casefile load speed.
- Improved suggestion flow, allowing for smoother expansions to the dialogue trees.
- Some previously broken achievements now work again.
- Name word blocks and "I" are now uppercase.
- Cleaned up a lot of typos.
- Installed tool to better catch future typos.

We also implemented over 100 user-submitted suggestions. Thank you so much for everyone submitted, will do a Hall of Heroes list in the next update, so your glory will never be forgotten.

Take care, and see you tomorrow for another update.

notes.title: Obligatory day one patch
notes.notes:
Hello all.

So, we survived the first 24 hours of the game launch, and we have gotten a ton of juicy feedback from you all. Let me start off by saying, I absolutely appreciate and love the responses and critiques we've had.

I promise you I will find the time to read through and reply to it all, and of course take all things into consideration.

I posted a small patch today, with the following tweaks:
- The Backspace key now (successfully) removes the last word in the sentence.
- The Delete key now flushes the entire sentence.
- Fixed loops where the AI would just repeat itself constantly.
- Tweaked some contradicting responses.
- The lingo processor is now a bit more accepting of incoming phrases, meaning that you can now reach a successful answer with a LOT more combinations.
- Fixed a bug where the game would sometimes not save progress properly.
- Fixed a ton of typos.

Also a great thanks to everyone submitting suggestions to missing sentences through the in-game menu. I will put it up and process it when I figure out a good way to do that.

That's all for me today, back to the writing desk for me.
